title: HP OmniBook X 173 LT AI
body: My wife and I needed new laptops that could run win 11.  After about a month of research I settled on this one.  We bought 2 and customized them a little.  We are 66 so wanted the largest screen we could get and these screens are large, 17in, and beautiful.  I ordered them with 32 gig of ram since we would not be able to upgrade later, also win 11 Pro.  They came with 3 USB ports although 1 more would have been nice.  The case is silver and feels solid. We wish they offered different colors so we could have picked what we wanted.  It is very fast although I haven't played any games on it.  The screen is gloss so you may have trouble if you plan on using it outside but we do not.  The only drawback I have is the keyboard.  The keys are flush with the surface of the case and really prefer they stick up a bit like my old laptop.  It's just to easy for me to make mistakes.  Overall I am happy and impressed with the laptop and would buy it again without hesitation.  I spent 20 years building and servicing computers in my own shop so I have some background to base my opinions on.

title: Pretty nice - 2 concerns
body:
Hi. The computer is fast and so far no problems. I like that is has 3 USB ports and an HDMI. I love the back-lit keyboard. Nice size SSD drive too.
-The keyboard keys being right next to each other is something I am no longer used to and results in accidentally pressing the adjacent keys sometimes (this didn't happen on the older type keyboards where there is a decent amount of space between the letters, it would have been nicer to have the spaces).
-The USB-C power cord concerns me. It doesn't feel as sturdy as the older round power cords and I am concerned that either the cord or the port will break.
-I would have preferred a matte screen - I don't need touch screen and it is much harder to see the screen if there is a window or other light behind me.

title: I/O Ports Excessively Tight Fit
body:
The laptop PC functions as advertised, with the following EXCEPTION: the USB and HDMI ports on the laptop are extremely "tight", so that it is physically very difficult to connect and disconnect external devices and cables to these ports. In fact, the physical "tightness" of the HDMI port is so problematic that the male connector portion of an external HDMI cable I had connected to this port sustained physical damage during disconnection of the cable from the HDMI port on the PC (i.e., the male connector portion of the HDMI cable physically separated from the HDMI cable itself while attempting to disconnect it from the port. After the "plug" portion of the cable separated from the cable itself, I actually had to use a pair of pliers to grip and remove the remnant "plug" portion of the external HDMI connector from the laptop HDMI port. It required a fair amount of pulling force using the pliers to remove the "stuck" portion of the external cable's plug-in connector from the laptop's HDMI port.) The referenced HDMI cable has been used with other devices I own without any problems in terms of connector fit and functionality. 

I will be investigating this problem further after I procure a replacement HDMI cable. (I cannot re-use the referenced cable, due to the damaged connector.) If this problem recurs with a new cable, I will be contacting HP for warranty repair/replacement of the HDMI port...this port should NOT "grip" the connector portion of an external HDMI cable so tightly that the cable connector sustains damage during disconnection.

body: This is a replacement for my old Envy HP laptop, 8 yrs old.  If I were to do it over again I would wish that the letters on the laptop were whiter and stand out more.  What I see is a weak white look and not as prominent as my keyboard is, so without the keyboard It will be a bit harder to see the letters.  Other than that little nit, this is a very nice laptop and I hope it lasts the next 8 years and the hinges don't fall off like my old one.  Take note HP fix the hinges or come up with a way to lubricate them.
